title: Use both acquired spectral moments and a zero atom before lifting a coherence bound
statement: A rank-one lower source and arbitrary PSD noise induce a probability law with E[S]=1/4 and E[q/(q+4S)]=1/2; its calibrated shifted-log inequality yields the exact positive-part coherence budget with k=log(32/27)/2.

requires: The actual rank-one spectral/resolvent receiver and compatible balanced two-source entropy transfer; q>0 uses the two exact moments, q=0 has a separate pointwise proof.
provides: A rank-one lower source and arbitrary PSD noise induce a probability law with E[S]=1/4 and E[q/(q+4S)]=1/2; its calibrated shifted-log inequality yields the exact positive-part coherence budget with k=log(32/27)/2.
assumptions: The law is not chosen independently of the matrix source. Add missing probability at S=0 rather than assume spectral weights sum to1. Rank(x)>=2 does not follow.
costs: Exact finite-dimensional entropy in nats and norm-convergent operator integrals; no runtime, state acquisition, instrument, physical implementation or practical advantage cost is supplied. Arbitrary dimension is a theorem quantifier, not computational efficiency.
contract.units: Entropy uses natural logarithms in nats; beta and rescaled H,V,r,s are dimensionless within the stated normalization. C is entropy lost under the declared block pinching, not an acquired physical cost.
contract.obstruction: Acquire/derive the needed source rank or operator cap in the intended receiving problem. Do not replace a matrix inequality by a trace bound or infer a measurement/decoder from the scalarization. Priority, devices and general WH3 remain unresolved.

body: Normalize x=|u><u| and y=x/4+3b/8. Positive spectral weights |<u,e_i>|^2/(4*s_i) sum to at most1; add their missing mass at0. The secular positive eigenvalue q of2x-4y gives the reciprocal calibration. Decompose the calibrated law into two-point laws on opposite sides of the harmonic center, prove the shifted-log bound by exact differentiation, mix using log concavity, and integrate in the upper scalar parameter. Spectral-filter Jensen followed by the existing balanced binary theorem controls all upper Schur remainders. The q=0 kernel proof and continuity/homogeneity close the remaining endpoints.
